Full source notes, evidence limitations, and direct Zotero links

  1. Julio Santilario-Berthilier, Antonio Calvo-Morata, Ivan Martinez-Ortiz, Marc Spaniol, and Baltasar Fernandez-Manjon. “[SIMVA: Serious Games Learning Analytics Based on Standards and Open Code](https://www.zotero.org/djgagnon/items/LS4U9RDW).” *Joint Proceedings of the Learning Analytics and Knowledge 2025 Workshops*, CEUR Workshop Proceedings, 2025. [Public full paper](https://ceur-ws.org/Vol-3995/GBLA25_paper1.pdf). Evidence: an open-source platform description and validation-oriented analytics workflow; not evidence that every generated metric measures learning.
  2. Sergej Görzen, Birte Heinemann, and Ulrik Schroeder. “[Evaluation of a Framework for the Integrating of Learning Analytics in Virtual Reality](https://www.zotero.org/djgagnon/items/SNR97HXI).” Gesellschaft für Informatik e.V., 2024. [DOI 10.18420/delfi2024-ws-16](https://doi.org/10.18420/delfi2024-ws-16). Evidence: an observation of seven computer-science students integrating analytics into VR; implementation and usability evidence, not a learning-gains trial.
  3. William L. Miller, Ryan S. Baker, Matthew J. Labrum, Karen Petsche, Yu-Han Liu, and Angela Z. Wagner. “[Automated Detection of Proactive Remediation by Teachers in Reasoning Mind Classrooms](https://www.zotero.org/djgagnon/items/Z4RME73N).” *Proceedings of the Fifth International Conference on Learning Analytics and Knowledge*, ACM, 2015. [DOI 10.1145/2723576.2723607](https://doi.org/10.1145/2723576.2723607). Evidence: a log-based detector of teacher remediation; inference is context-sensitive and generalization is limited.
  4. Philip I. Pavlik Jr., Hao Cen, and Kenneth R. Koedinger. “[Performance Factors Analysis—A New Alternative to Knowledge Tracing](https://www.zotero.org/djgagnon/items/CP694EPH).” *Proceedings of the 14th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Education*, *Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications* 200, IOS Press, 2009, pp. 531–538. [DOI 10.3233/978-1-60750-028-5-531](https://doi.org/10.3233/978-1-60750-028-5-531). Evidence: a model comparison for educational data mining and adaptive practice; not proof of broad classroom benefit.
  5. Ryan Baker, Caitlin Mills, and Jaeyoon Choi. “[The Difficulty of Achieving High Precision with Low Base Rates for High-Stakes Intervention](https://www.zotero.org/djgagnon/items/R4GVL9SN).” *Proceedings of the 15th International Learning Analytics and Knowledge Conference*, ACM, 2025. [DOI 10.1145/3706468.3706477](https://doi.org/10.1145/3706468.3706477). Evidence: a methodological demonstration about prevalence, precision, and error costs; not an intervention trial.
  6. Asmalina Saleh, Chen Yuxin, Cindy E. Hmelo-Silver, Krista D. Glazewski, Bradford W. Mott, and James C. Lester. “[Coordinating Scaffolds for Collaborative Inquiry in a Game-Based Learning Environment](https://www.zotero.org/djgagnon/items/XDYFELXE).” *Journal of Research in Science Teaching*, 2020. [DOI 10.1002/tea.21656](https://doi.org/10.1002/tea.21656). Evidence: game-based collaborative-inquiry and scaffolding research; the episode does not claim more than the source supports.
